The Redis profile cache stores select_first_name, i.e. the value of whichever source was active when it was written (with hide applied) — not always the Aisle-DB name.

The profile cache is only stored for approved, pending, disapproved and vip_disapproved profiles (allowed_for_cache?, profile.rb:6009); pending_not_verified accounts are always a cache miss. A nil PII result is never cached.
The CMS likes filter (FN-CMS-014) is not a Postgres bypass: it calls get_first_name on a UserLike row (probable 500).
A-R7 (PII then Postgres fallback) behaviour exists in Aisle at FN-AIS-071 (current_first_name = get_first_name || first_name, profile.rb:3376), filed under A-W1.

normalize_first_name keeps the original value when nothing Latin is left ("123", emoji) and cuts mixed names ("José" → "Jos"); the 1-character initial rule also applies to users who are not hidden; profile_first_name_source skips clean-up.
Plaintext names in the Aisle DB are by design (A-X16 is context, not a risk).
POST /V1/pii_integration/profile_first_name_source exists on develop_new and works on staging (seen 2026-11-09).

Vernac differs from Aisle: with no PII NAME the getter falls back to Postgres (direct_fields.rb:10), pending_not_verified profiles are cached (profile.rb:2181), and chat lists are re-hydrated on every read (ConversationHydrator).
Vernac DB view profile_view (desiapp test DB) copies account_profiles.first_name in plain text; no app code reads it — downstream reader unknown (M2FNQ-50).

Postgres schema scan (2026-11-12, schema and JSON key names only, see postgres-name-columns.md): user names are held in profiles.first_name / account_profiles.first_name, the profile_view views, chat_requests.profile_data_json, offline_event_orders.personal_info.name (both DBs) and paint_bar_mixers.personal_details.name (Aisle; new row for its route). payment_paypal_transactions.first_name/last_name and user_test_data.first_name exist in the Aisle DB but no code on develop_new writes them (legacy).
